questions.question: Comprehension:Read the given passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.The Indus Valley Civilisation, which flourished around 2500 BCE, is regarded as one of the earliest urban societies in human history. Spanning parts of present-day India and Pakistan, it was remarkable for its advanced city planning, drainage systems, and standardised brick structures. Cities like Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro were laid out on a grid pattern, with wide streets and sophisticated public baths—features that reflected an organised and progressive society.Archaeologists have discovered seals, pottery, tools, and jewelry that reveal the artistic and commercial achievements of this civilisation. Trade links with Mesopotamia suggest that the Indus people had a well-developed system of exchange. Interestingly, the script used by them remains undeciphered even today, leaving many aspects of their language, beliefs, and governance shrouded in mystery.Around 1900 BCE, the civilisation began to decline, possibly due to environmental changes such as shifting river courses or repeated floods. Despite its fall, the Indus Valley left an enduring legacy of urban culture, technological skill, and social organisation. Its silent ruins continue to remind us that even in ancient times, human ingenuity could build cities of remarkable complexity and order, inspiring modern planners and historians to appreciate the sophistication and enduring wisdom of early civilisations and their contribution to human progress.Q76. Which feature shows that the Indus people were skilled city planners?
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'A' (Grid-patterned streets and drainage systems) है।
